lessons.title: How Flag Works
lessons.blurb: Flags, no blocking, and three plays to get there.

steps.title: Five on five
steps.body: In NFL FLAG, most games are five players against five. Every player wears a belt with flags. Pulling the ball carrier's flag ends the play, like a tackle. Your league may change a few rules, so ask your coach.

steps.title: No blocking, no fumbles
steps.body: Nobody blocks or tackles in flag. The ball carrier can't push hands away or cover their flags; that's a penalty called flag guarding. If the ball hits the ground, the play is over. There are no fumbles.

steps.prompt: In NFL FLAG, the runner pushes a defender's hand away from their flag. What is that?
steps.explanation: Runners can't protect their flags with a hand, an arm or the ball. That's flag guarding.

steps.statement: In NFL FLAG, if the runner drops the ball, the defense can pick it up and run.
steps.explanation: There are no fumbles in NFL FLAG. The play ends, and the ball goes where the runner's feet were.

steps.title: Three plays at a time
steps.body: There are no kickoffs or punts. A team starts on its own 5-yard line and gets 3 plays to cross midfield, then 3 more to score. Just before midfield and just before the goal line are no-run zones. From there, you have to pass.

steps.prompt: Your team gets the ball in NFL FLAG. How many plays do you get to cross midfield?
steps.explanation: Three plays to cross midfield, then three more to score.

steps.prompt: The ball is in the no-run zone near the goal line. What does the offense have to do?
steps.explanation: In a no-run zone, the offense has to pass to score or cross midfield.

lessons.title: Rushing and Scoring
lessons.blurb: The 7-yard rush, who can catch, and points after.

steps.title: Rushing the passer
steps.body: Defenders who rush the quarterback start 7 yards back from the line, and nobody may touch the quarterback. The quarterback can't run past the line but can hand off behind it. Every player on offense can catch a pass, even the center.

steps.title: Points after a touchdown
steps.body: A touchdown is 6 points, and there's no kick after it. The offense gets one play from the 5-yard line for 1 point, or from the 10 for 2. The 5 is in the no-run zone, so the 1-point try has to be a pass.

steps.prompt: In NFL FLAG, where does a defender start to rush the quarterback?
steps.explanation: Rushers start 7 yards back, so the quarterback has time to throw.

steps.statement: In NFL FLAG, a try from the 10-yard line after a touchdown is worth 2 points.
steps.explanation: From the 5 it's 1 point; from the farther 10 it's 2.

steps.prompt: In NFL FLAG, who can catch a pass?
choices: Only the receivers and the running back
steps.explanation: Every offensive player can catch a pass in NFL FLAG, even the center. The quarterback can too, after handing the ball off.

steps.prompt: In NFL FLAG, can the quarterback run past the line with the ball?
choices: No, but they can hand it off behind the line
steps.explanation: The quarterback can't run past the line, but a handoff behind it is fine.
